Are password changes and profile-image edits required through /api/user, given A9's report that password is not forwarded and image is read-only? Provide expected success and rejection examples.

For ArticleViewSet.update and comment DELETE, may anyone other than the author change content, and must a comment ID belong to the supplied article slug? Provide allow/deny examples for authors, other users and moderators.

For upgrading Django 1.10.5, Django REST Framework 3.4.4 and PyJWT 1.4.2 flagged by A6, what remediation deadline, API compatibility constraints and regression evidence are required, and is client token invalidation acceptable during rollout?

On account deletion, should Profile, Articles, Comments, favorites and follow relationships be deleted, anonymized or retained, and how should public attribution and backups be handled? Please supply the approved dataset-specific policy rather than the scripted retention answer.

Should the authentication app retain its 60-day JWT lifetime, and what must happen to existing tokens after password changes, deactivation or compromise? What client re-login disruption is acceptable?

Which clients actively use /api/articles/feed, article filters, favorites and profile-follow endpoints? Supply dated usage evidence, compatibility-critical journeys and expected feed responses to resolve the reported routing uncertainty.

For /api/articles, /api/articles/feed, direct article reads, comments and /api/tags, should non-demo users see each other's content? Please approve a visibility matrix for anonymous callers, authors, followers and other users.
Is the 60-day JWT lifetime intentional, and what must happen to existing tokens after password changes, account deletion or suspected compromise?
Must old /api/articles/:slug links work after title changes, and should edits omitting tagList preserve tags? Which client acceptance tests establish these expectations?

On account deletion, what should happen to the Prisma User, authored articles/comments, favorites and follow relationships, and should article deletion always cascade to comments? What deadlines and verification criteria apply?
Which actual clients depend on login, article publishing, followed-author feeds and comments, and what dated volume, error and latency metrics should determine migration acceptance priority?

For A6's Tomcat and Spring MVC matches, are DIGEST/FORM authentication, SSE fragment rendering or XsltView enabled in deployment? Please supply configuration evidence and specify required patch regression checks and exception approval.
If an owner has two pets with the same name, including case-only differences, should PetController reject the second pet or allow disambiguation, and how should existing duplicates be migrated?
Should Owner telephone fields remain exactly ten digits, or support international numbers and extensions? Which registration examples must acceptance tests cover?

The scripted answer describes emails and password hashes, while discovery maps owners, pets and visits. Which datasets exist in the deployed application or external identity system, and how should deleting owner contact information affect linked pets, visit descriptions and backups?

VisitController accepts future dates only: must staff also record same-day treatment or historical visits, and which clinic timezone should set the date boundary? Please provide accepted and rejected examples.
Who actually performs owner search, owner edits and visit creation, and which journey causes the most rework? Can you supply a dated walkthrough and representative usage counts or support cases?
For /export_posts through RQ and email, should success mean job completion, mail-provider acceptance or recipient delivery, and what deadline, retry behavior and failure message are required?
For /translate, which user-submitted text may be sent to Microsoft Translator, is the documented westus region acceptable, and what notice, redaction or opt-out is required?
Must POST /api/users enforce the same email and password validation as browser registration, and do existing API clients constrain tightening these rules?
Should opening one page of /messages mark all earlier messages as read or only displayed messages, and how should unread counts behave across devices?
When Elasticsearch is absent, unavailable or behind SQL posts, should /search be disabled, show a degraded-service notice or offer a fallback, and what post-indexing lag is acceptable?
Which of posting/feed reading, direct messaging, password recovery and emailed exports must pass migration acceptance first, and can you provide usage and failure telemetry supporting that ranking?

For /api/profiles/:username/follow, must self-follow always be rejected, and should repeated follow or unfollow requests succeed idempotently or return errors? Please provide expected status codes and resulting relationship state for each case.

For recovery of User/Profile links, article authors, comments, favorites and follows, what reconciliation checks must pass before reopening writes, and can you supply the latest dated restore exercise with measured data loss and recovery time?

Have any nonlocal conduit deployments used the checked-in SECRET_KEY or DEBUG=True? Supply redacted configuration provenance and secret-rotation history, without disclosing secret values, and identify the incident-review process if exposure is found.

Is SQLite in conduit/settings.py the deployed store for User, Profile, Article, Comment and Tag, or only a development default? Provide a redacted environment-to-database inventory and explain how schema migrations and write cutover are currently performed.

What response-time and payload-size acceptance budgets apply to article listing and feed retrieval, and what measured article/tag/favorite/follow distributions and page sizes should a representative load test use?

Which revision of the external RealWorld API specification is normative for this app, and are the custom JSON envelopes and validation/not-found errors in conduit/apps/core intentional deviations? Provide approved request/response fixtures for registration and article/comment errors.

For /owners/find, should a blank last name list all owners, and how should prefix search handle case, accents and families sharing a surname? Please provide expected results for representative searches and confirm whether five-record pages are acceptable.

For /owners/{ownerId}, owner edits and nested pet/visit routes, may every staff member read and modify every owner's records, or are records restricted by clinic or role? Please provide allowed and denied examples and identify where deployment enforces them.

How should staff register a pet whose type is absent from PetTypeRepository, and what should happen to existing pets when a reference type is renamed or retired? Please describe the approved correction workflow.

VisitController displays 'Your visit has been booked' without allocating a veterinarian or time slot. Is this entry a confirmed appointment or a request, and what external scheduling step, if any, must occur before staff can promise attendance?

Who or what consumes the unpaginated /vets response, and how quickly must changes to veterinarians or specialties appear in /vets and /vets.html despite caching? Please supply consumer examples and acceptable stale-data scenarios.

For API /users, /users/<id>, and follower/following lists, which profile fields and relationship data should an authenticated user be allowed to see about other users, and are there private-account or blocking scenarios that migration acceptance must cover?

For microblog's web and worker deployment, when was the last end-to-end restore rehearsal, which persistent stores and queued work were restored, and what measured recovery time and data loss did the exercise demonstrate?

Which clients use the API /tokens issuance and revocation routes, and must existing tokens remain valid across cutover, password reset and browser logout; what revocation acceptance tests should those clients pass?

Which production deployment actually runs microblog: the Dockerfile/boot.sh path, the Procfile web and worker processes, or another setup, and can you provide deployment configuration plus web/worker CPU, memory and queue-depth measurements over a representative peak period?

For conduit/apps/authentication/backends.py, what status and error body must clients receive for a signed JWT missing id, an invalid id type, an unsupported signing algorithm or a deleted-user id? Supply approved negative request/response fixtures and specify whether any existing client depends on distinct error messages.

For conduit/manage.py and requirements.txt, can the maintainer demonstrate a clean checkout-to-running-API bootstrap, including interpreter/platform, dependency resolution, migrations and registration/login smoke checks, and supply dated logs plus any external build scripts omitted from this repository?

Is the scripted assertion that email delivery is the only outbound dependency true for any deployed conduit environment? If so, which registration, recovery or notification journey sends email, where is that implementation configured, and what redacted provider/failure evidence supports it; if not, can an authorized respondent mark it simulation-only?

What authoritative license or permission permits reuse and redistribution of django-realworld-example-app, and can the release/legal reviewer provide the repository license provenance and dependency-license review for the six requirements.txt packages before packaging a migrated release?

Does any deployed registration, login or account-update workflow actually send email? If so, identify the sending component, provider, trigger and failure behavior, and supply configuration or trace evidence without credentials.

For auth.ts and token.utils.ts, can the deployment/security representative provide redacted evidence that every deployed environment supplies JWT_SECRET and describe the required startup behavior if it is missing or empty?

For the Prisma PostgreSQL database, what backup and point-in-time recovery mechanisms exist, and can operations provide the latest dated restore exercise showing recoverable data and measured recovery time?

Is GET / consumed by a load balancer, uptime monitor or client, and which response contract is approved: the e2e test's message response or src/main.ts's status response? Should this endpoint indicate process liveness only or database readiness?

When clients retry article/comment creation or favorite/follow operations after a timeout, what duplicate-handling and response behavior is required, and which client scenarios should be added to acceptance tests?

Which environments execute src/prisma/seed.ts, and must generated demo User, Article, Comment and Tag data be retained, regenerated or excluded during migration? How will real accounts and their relationships be distinguished from demo records?

For the Thymeleaf owner and pet forms, which languages, browsers and assistive technologies must be supported, and can a representative demonstrate keyboard-only completion and understanding of validation errors for the required combinations?

If submitting /owners/new or a new visit times out before staff see confirmation, how should staff determine whether it saved, and what duplicate-prevention or recovery behavior must the UI provide on retry?

If two staff members open /owners/{ownerId}/edit and save different telephone or address changes, should the second save overwrite, merge or require review? Please give an accepted conflict-resolution example.
When changing the Petclinic database profile or schema, what reconciliation checks on owners, linked pets and visits must pass before staff resume work, and what failed check should trigger rollback?

Which of the H2, MySQL or PostgreSQL profiles holds operational owner, pet and visit records, and what must remain unchanged after an application restart or SQL initialization? Please provide deployment configuration and a restart acceptance example.
